# Istravex

> Open-source XDR conformance and replay kit for Stellar. Checks that SDKs decode and re-encode XDR faithfully, and that indexers store the right records for the right accounts, using a shared, versioned corpus of rare but valid Stellar XDR. Proposed for Stellar Community Fund (SCF) #46, RFP 2. Status: proposed for funding; a working kit (corpus, provenance verifier, SDK runners, mock RPC, replay, Go linter, upstream pilot) is in the repository.

## Docs

- [Repository](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex): site, corpus, capture scripts, runners, replay harness
- [Corpus format](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/tree/main/corpus): manifest schema and fixtures
- [Full proposal (Markdown)](/proposal.md): scope, problem, deliverables, draft manifest, milestones, maintenance
- [SCF RFP Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/rfp-track): official RFP scope

## Corpus and results (real data)

- 137 fixtures: 95 mainnet, 30 testnet, 10 generated on a pinned stellar-core, 2 synthetic (labelled; bytes a decoder must refuse). 20 hand-written patterns that broke real software; 116 chosen by set cover so that all 470 XDR cells real traffic uses are in the corpus; 1 captured by name for a finding
  - shape-scan read 400,311 mainnet and testnet ledgers (59.6 million transactions) from SDF's public data lake; 470 of 603 reachable cells (union arms, flag bits, contract cost types) occur; the corpus covers all 470 (corpus/cells.json)
  - CAP coverage: 45 of the 47 live CAPs with a ledger shape; the other 23 live CAPs leave none (host functions, consensus, buckets), each with the reason; open: CAP-0070, CAP-0083
  - hand-written patterns include: cap27-muxed-payment-pubnet-0001/0002 (muxed IDs above 2^53 and 2^63), cap15-fee-bump-pubnet-0001, cap40-signed-payload-signer (reproduces wallet-backend#729), cap73-sac-trust (wallet-backend#731), cap27-muxed-max-id-local-0001 (js-stellar-sdk#1785), cap46-muxed-soroban-source-local-0001 (wallet-backend#716), cap38-pool-issuer-order-local-0001 (js-stellar-sdk#1766), cap46-scmap-host-order-local-0001 (#1766, #1789), base-max-amount-local-0001 (stellar-etl#454), base-memo-non-utf8, max-length vectors, over-max-length and hostile ScVal limits
- Generated cases: 45,144 valid and hostile values (trailing bytes, truncation, bad first word) of every XDR type, deterministic from a seed, through every SDK; stellar-core 30.0.0 print-xdr is the oracle (672/672); with the corpus they reach all 603 reachable cells (https://docs.istravex.com/tools/generated-cases)
- Provenance: 1,808/1,808 checks; every non-synthetic fixture is byte-identical to the canonical LedgerCloseMeta of its ledger
- SDK conformance: 2,810/2,816 checks across seven SDKs: @stellar/stellar-sdk 17.4.0, go-stellar-sdk 0.9.0, stellar-xdr 30.0.0 (Rust), Python stellar-sdk 17.0.1 and stellar-xdr 0.2.1, java-stellar-sdk 6.0.0, stellar-php-sdk 1.18.0; every failure is a finding; js-stellar-sdk 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 fail exactly the checks for #1766, #1785 and #1789
- Sweep: Go, Rust, JavaScript, Python and Java over 1,241 whole ledgers; every ledger round-trips byte for byte and each of 310,837 transaction hashes is checked against stellar-core's; Go, JavaScript, Rust and Python match every hash; Java gets 58 mainnet hashes wrong (F-0023)
- Replay: the naive indexer is wrong on 9/9 cases; the reference indexer is right on 9/9; ledgers served over mock RPC getLedgers or the Galexie data-lake layout (filesystem or S3)
- Upstream pilots: stellar/wallet-backend @ 3e22515 indexes 123/123 fixtures correctly over RPC and over the data lake; stellar/stellar-horizon v30.0.1, through its own db reingest range into PostgreSQL, gets 123/123; stellar-etl v2.8.35 gets 119/123, the misses its open issues #454 and #460; wallet-backend#729, #731 and #716 reproduce on the commits before their fixes
- Findings: 28 in corpus/findings.json (https://api.istravex.com/v1/findings): 9 new defects, all filed upstream (stellar-core#5507, #5508; js-stellar-sdk#1906; java-stellar-sdk#844; stellar-php-sdk#220 to #224), 15 known bugs reproduced, 4 notes
- RFP sightings: 13 of 18 reproduced in CI (before and after the fix, or on the current release where it is unreleased), 3 exercised, 2 not covered with the reason (https://docs.istravex.com/corpus/sightings)
- Hardening guide: https://docs.istravex.com/guide/overview (draft; review by a stellar-core engineer requested); field-by-field table at https://docs.istravex.com/guide/validated-fields
- stellar-core goldens: JavaScript, Go and Rust round-trip 15,306/15,306 LedgerCloseMeta frames from core's --check-lcm data (v30.0.0)
- Docs: https://docs.istravex.com
- Threat model and monitoring plan: https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/blob/main/THREAT-MODEL.md (SDF template, STRIDE); releases carry SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance
- Security policy: https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/blob/main/SECURITY.md (private vulnerability reporting; exploitable findings disclosed privately first via SDF's bug bounty)
- Guides: https://docs.istravex.com/guides/sdk-conformance (SDK), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/indexer-ci (indexer CI), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/fixtures-in-tests (app tests), https://docs.istravex.com/guides/hosted-api (API)
- API: https://api.istravex.com (OpenAPI: https://api.istravex.com/openapi.json)
- Mock Stellar RPC: https://rpc.istravex.com/{pubnet,testnet,local}

## Deliverables

1. Versioned XDR corpus + CAP coverage audit (captured ledgers and pinned stellar-core recipes; synthetic entries labelled; checked against `--check-lcm` goldens where available)
2. Offline indexer replay harness (mock Stellar RPC `getLedgers`, reference adapter for `wallet-backend`; verdicts: correct, incorrect, dropped)
3. Cross-SDK conformance runner (pinned JavaScript, Go, Rust adapters; decode, byte-for-byte re-encode, native conversion checks; wide integers kept at full precision)
4. Go linter (3 rules: trusting Core pass-through fields; unbounded recursive XDR; participants derived from the envelope instead of ledger meta) + indexer-hardening guide
5. Upstream pilot against `wallet-backend` with a triaged findings report

## Manifest fields

id, cap_ids, protocol_version, network, xdr_type, xdr_path, sha256, source, synthetic, expected_decoded, expected_indexed. Wide integers are decimal strings.

## Milestones

1. Corpus and reference replay
2. Conformance and linting
3. Upstream pilot and public release

## Commitments (proposed)

Apache 2.0; maintained by Istravex Labs for 12 months from the award, through the first protocol upgrade after delivery; no usage telemetry.
